headline: High: kotaemon’s broad egress and file/API handling can leak or misapply data when paired with a non-runnable awesome-nlp list that offers no isolation or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-nlp is non-runnable and exposes no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest kotaemon output. kotaemon uses a web UI and file-backed app data, but without a shared channel or parser bridge, the pairwise prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem or copy-paste bridge is added between the two agents, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF kotaemon is configured to parse content from awesome-nlp as instructions, the risk changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any automatic import of text from awesome-nlp into kotaemon prompts.
Use manual review before copying content between them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon touches documents, transcripts, and API keys and can call external APIs; awesome-nlp has no runtime or data surfaces, so it is not a leak source itself. The pair still creates a leakage path if shared files or copied content move sensitive documents into kotaemon’s broad egress pipeline.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace containing sensitive documents, kotaemon can transmit them to third-party APIs.
IF API keys are present in files accessible to kotaemon, those secrets may be exposed through its document-processing flow.
mitigations: Store secrets outside any shared folder.
Separate the agents into distinct directories.
Disable external API backends in kotaemon for sensitive runs.
Review uploads before indexing them in kotaemon.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write or network capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. kotaemon supports multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data, but the pair lacks a documented shared writable target, making conflict possible only under unusual co-location.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file contention can occur.
IF an operator runs multiple kotaemon instances against one app-data path, state collisions become possible.
mitigations: Assign unique data directories per instance.
Avoid mounting the same folder into both agents.
Run only one kotaemon instance per workspace.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-nlp is a static list, so it does not generate authoritative facts; kotaemon, however, can ingest documents and render outputs from them. If operators treat imported content as authoritative without verification, kotaemon can propagate errors from copied or indexed material even though the upstream agent is non-runnable.
conditions: IF content from awesome-nlp is manually copied into kotaemon as source material, kotaemon may present it without verification.
IF kotaemon is used to answer support questions from unvetted documents, downstream actions may rely on incorrect material.
mitigations: Require human verification of imported sources.
Label copied content as untrusted in kotaemon.
Use a review step before any customer-facing response.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented for awesome-nlp, while kotaemon explicitly handles documents and API keys and may send data to external APIs. Because only kotaemon has compliance-relevant surfaces, the pairwise issue is limited to operator-controlled handling rather than a proven cross-agent violation.
conditions: IF regulated documents are indexed in kotaemon and external APIs are enabled, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF secrets are stored in files that kotaemon ingests, retention and access controls must cover them.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from kotaemon indexes.
Use local-only backends for sensitive workloads.
Document retention settings for app data.
Keep API keys in a separate secret store.
